string-array.name: descriptionShouldersOneArmMedicineBallSlam
string-array.item: One Arm Medicine Ball Slam
A dynamic exercise that builds power, coordination, and upper body strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball in one hand.
2. Lift the ball overhead, fully extending your arm.
3. Using explosive power, slam the ball down onto the ground as hard as possible.
4. Catch the ball on the rebound or pick it up, and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core and avoid rounding your back during the slam.
2. Perform the movement with controlled aggression to maximize power.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersSeatedBarbellShoulderPress
string-array.item: Seated Barbell Shoulder Press
A compound exercise to target the shoulders, triceps, and upper chest.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on a bench with back support, holding a barbell at shoulder height with an overhand grip.
2. Press the barbell overhead until your arms are fully extended.
3. Lower the barbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back pressed against the bench and avoid arching excessively.
2. Lower the barbell just below chin level for a full range of motion.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersMedicineBallOverheadThrow
string-array.item: Medicine Ball Overhead Throw
An explosive exercise to develop upper body strength and power.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball with both hands.
2. Lift the ball overhead, extending your arms fully.
3. Using explosive power, throw the ball forward or against a wall as hard as possible.
4. Retrieve the ball and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use your entire body to generate force, including your legs and core.
2. Maintain a neutral spine and avoid overextending your lower back.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellPushPress
string-array.item: Dumbbell Push Press
A compound movement that targets the shoulders, triceps, and legs, while developing explosive power.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing forward.
2. Slightly bend your knees and use your legs to help press the dumbbells overhead.
3. Fully extend your arms overhead, then lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the press.
2. Keep your movements controlled and avoid excessive swinging of the weights.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersStandingDumbbellShoulderPress
string-array.item: Standing Dumbbell Shoulder Press
A basic yet effective exercise to strengthen the shoulders, triceps, and upper chest.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing forward.
2. Press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
3. Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height in a controlled manner.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and prevent arching your lower back.
2. Move the dumbbells in a smooth and controlled motion to maximize effectiveness.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersArmScissors
string-array.item: Arm Scissors
A dynamic stretch to improve shoulder mobility and warm up the upper body.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms extended straight out to the sides at shoulder height.
2. Swing your arms in front of your body, crossing them like scissors.
3. Open your arms wide again, returning to the starting position.
4. Repeat the movement in a continuous and fluid motion.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging during the movement.
2. Perform the exercise at a moderate pace to avoid straining your muscles.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersSideArmRaises
string-array.item: Side Arm Raises
An isolation exercise to target the lateral deltoids for stronger and more defined shoulders.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand or sit with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding dumbbells in each hand by your sides.
2. Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
3. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum; focus on controlled movements.
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbows to reduce strain on your joints.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersArmCircles
string-array.item: Arm Circles
A simple exercise to warm up the shoulders, improve mobility, and increase blood flow.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height.
2. Make small forward circles with your arms in a continuous motion.
3. After a set number of repetitions, reverse the direction of the circles.
4. Repeat as desired.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your movements controlled and consistent.
2. Avoid shrugging your shoulders during the exercise.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellLateralRaise
string-array.item: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
A key isolation exercise for building strong and defined lateral deltoids.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand or sit with a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides with palms facing inward.
2. Lift the dumbbells out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
3. Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid swinging the dumbbells or using momentum.
2. Focus on engaging your shoulder muscles throughout the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellShoulderPress
string-array.item: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
A compound exercise to strengthen the shoulders, triceps, and upper chest.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit or stand with a dumbbell in each hand, holding them at shoulder height with palms facing forward.
2. Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended.
3. Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to maintain stability.
2. Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersSmithMachineBehindNeckPress
string-array.item: Smith Machine Behind Neck Press
An exercise targeting the shoulders, specifically the deltoids, with added stability from the Smith machine.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on a bench placed under the Smith machine, with the barbell positioned at shoulder height behind your neck.
2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width, with palms facing forward.
3. Unlock the bar and slowly lower it behind your head to just above shoulder level.
4. Press the bar upward until your arms are fully extended.
5. Lower the bar back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and avoid excessive arching.
2. Perform the movement in a controlled manner to avoid straining your shoulders.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersSmithMachineShoulderPress
string-array.item: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
A compound exercise for developing shoulder strength and size with support from the Smith machine.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on a bench with a backrest positioned under the Smith machine, with the bar at shoulder height.
2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width, palms facing forward.
3. Unlock the bar and press it upward until your arms are fully extended.
4. Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position at shoulder level.
5. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to maintain proper posture.
2. Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersCableLateralRaise
string-array.item: Cable Lateral Raise
An isolation exercise for the lateral deltoids, helping to build shoulder width and definition.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand next to a cable machine with the handle attachment set at the lowest position.
2. Grab the handle with the hand farthest from the machine, and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
3. Keeping a slight bend in your elbow, raise your arm laterally until it reaches shoulder height.
4. Lower the handle back to the starting position in a controlled motion.
5. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum or swinging your body.
2. Focus on engaging your deltoid muscles throughout the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionShoulders45DegreeInclineRow
string-array.item: 45 Degree Incline Row
A compound exercise targeting the rear deltoids, traps, and upper back muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set an adjustable bench to a 45-degree incline and lie chest-down on it.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended toward the ground.
3. Pull the dumbbells toward your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
5. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid letting your elbows flare out too much.
2. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together during each rep.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersLeverShoulderPress
string-array.item: Lever Shoulder Press
A machine-based exercise for building strength and size in the shoulders, especially the deltoids.
To perform the exercise:
1. Adjust the seat height of the lever shoulder press machine so the handles are at shoulder level.
2. Sit down and grip the handles with palms facing forward.
3. Push the handles upward until your arms are fully extended.
4. Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back firmly pressed against the seat to avoid strain.
2. Perform the movement in a controlled manner to maximize effectiveness.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersStandingCloseGripMilitaryPress
string-array.item: Standing Close Grip Military Press
A shoulder exercise that emphasizes the anterior deltoids and triceps by using a narrow grip on the barbell.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with a close grip (hands slightly narrower than shoulder-width).
2. Bring the barbell to shoulder level, resting it on your upper chest.
3. Press the barbell upward until your arms are fully extended above your head.
4. Lower the barbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
5. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to avoid arching your back.
2. Ensure the barbell travels in a straight line for maximum efficiency.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersBarbellMilitaryPress
string-array.item: Barbell Military Press (Overhead Press)
A classic compound movement for building shoulder strength and stability, targeting the deltoids, triceps, and upper chest.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with a barbell held at shoulder level, palms facing forward and elbows slightly forward.
2. Press the barbell upward in a straight line until your arms are fully extended.
3. Lower the barbell back to the starting position at shoulder level.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid leaning back; keep your core tight to maintain stability.
2. Use a grip slightly wider than shoulder-width for optimal engagement.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellChestSupportedLateralRaises
string-array.item: Dumbbell Chest Supported Lateral Raises
An isolation exercise that targets the lateral deltoids while minimizing momentum.
To perform the exercise:
1. Adjust a bench to a slight incline and lie chest-down on it.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, allowing your arms to hang down naturally.
3. Lift the dumbbells outward to shoulder height, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep the movement controlled to avoid using momentum.
2. Focus on squeezing your shoulder muscles at the top of the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbell6WayRaise
string-array.item: Dumbbell 6 Way Raise
An advanced shoulder exercise that targets all deltoid heads through a combination of movements.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Raise the dumbbells laterally to shoulder height.
3. Move the dumbbells forward in front of you, then lift them overhead.
4. Reverse the motion by lowering the dumbbells back to shoulder height in front of you, moving them laterally, and finally returning to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use light weights to maintain control and proper form.
2. Keep your movements slow and deliberate to maximize shoulder engagement.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbell4WayLateralRaise
string-array.item: Dumbbell 4 Way Lateral Raise
A challenging variation of the lateral raise that engages all areas of the deltoids.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Perform a lateral raise, lifting the dumbbells to shoulder height.
3. Bring the dumbbells forward to meet in front of your chest.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to your sides and repeat.
5. Continue for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
2. Avoid swinging the weights; focus on controlled motion.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersAlternatingDumbbellFrontRaise
string-array.item: Alternating Dumbbell Front Raise
A shoulder exercise that targets the anterior deltoids while improving shoulder stability and coordination.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs.
2. Lift one dumbbell in front of you to shoulder height, keeping your arm straight.
3. Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position while raising the other dumbbell.
4. Alternate arms for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum; keep the movement controlled.
2. Do not lift the dumbbell above shoulder height to reduce strain on the shoulder joint.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersTwoArmCableFrontRaise
string-array.item: Two Arm Cable Front Raise
An isolation exercise that focuses on the anterior deltoids using cables for consistent tension.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach handles to the low pulleys of a cable machine and stand between them.
2. Hold the handles with palms facing down and arms straight in front of your thighs.
3. Raise both handles simultaneously to shoulder height.
4. Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your arms straight but not locked at the elbows.
2. Engage your core to maintain stability and avoid swaying.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersTwoArmDumbbellFrontRaise
string-array.item: Two Arm Dumbbell Front Raise
A simple yet effective exercise for targeting the anterior deltoids.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms in front of your thighs, palms facing down.
2. Raise both dumbbells simultaneously to shoulder height.
3. Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and avoid leaning backward.
2. Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the set.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellFrontRaise
string-array.item: Dumbbell Front Raise
A classic anterior deltoid exercise that also engages the upper chest and traps.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your thighs.
2. Lift both dumbbells in front of you to shoulder height, keeping your arms straight.
3. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain control throughout the movement to avoid swinging.
2. Stop at shoulder height to protect your shoulder joints.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersCableFrontRaise
string-array.item: Cable Front Raise
A variation of the front raise that uses a cable machine for continuous tension on the anterior deltoids.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach a straight bar or handle to the low pulley of a cable machine.
2. Stand upright facing the machine and hold the bar with both hands, palms facing down.
3. Raise the bar in front of you to shoulder height.
4. Lower the bar back to the starting position in a controlled motion.
5. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to maintain a stable posture.
2. Use a moderate weight to avoid jerky movements.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersLeaningSingleArmDumbbellLateralRaise
string-array.item: Leaning Single Arm Dumbbell Lateral Raise
A shoulder isolation exercise that targets the lateral deltoids with an extended range of motion.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in one hand and use the other hand to grip a stable support at hip height.
2. Lean your body away from the support, allowing your arm holding the dumbbell to hang straight down.
3. Raise the dumbbell out to the side until your arm is parallel to the ground.
4. Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum; perform the movement slowly and under control.
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbow to reduce strain on the joint.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersSeatedBehindNeckPress
string-array.item: Seated Behind Neck Press
A shoulder pressing exercise that emphasizes the rear and lateral deltoids.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on a bench with a barbell held behind your head at shoulder level, palms facing forward.
2. Press the barbell upward until your arms are fully extended.
3. Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position behind your neck.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use a controlled motion to avoid straining your shoulders or neck.
2. Keep your back straight and avoid arching during the press.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersRearDeltFlyMachine
string-array.item: Rear Delt Fly Machine
A machine-based exercise that targets the rear deltoids, traps, and upper back muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Adjust the machine\'s seat and handles to align with your shoulders.
2. Sit on the machine, gripping the handles with palms facing inward.
3. Pull the handles outward and backward, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Focus on using your rear deltoids rather than your arms.
2. Avoid jerking or swinging the handles.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersSeatedRearLateralDumbbellRaise
string-array.item: Seated Rear Lateral Dumbbell Raise
A free-weight exercise targeting the rear deltoids and upper back.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other.
2. Lean forward slightly so that your chest is near your thighs.
3. Lift the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor.
4. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
2. Focus on engaging the rear deltoids rather than using momentum.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersHalfArnoldPress
string-array.item: Half Arnold Press
A shoulder pressing variation that combines the Arnold Press and a half-rep for added intensity.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level with your palms facing your chest.
2. Rotate your palms outward and press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended.
3. Lower the dumbbells halfway down, then press them back up to the top.
4. Finally, lower the dumbbells completely back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use a weight that allows you to maintain control throughout the exercise.
2. Engage your core to stabilize your body and prevent leaning.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersArnoldPress
string-array.item: Arnold Press
A compound shoulder exercise that targets the front, side, and rear deltoids, along with engaging the triceps.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing your chest.
2. Rotate your wrists outward as you press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
3. Reverse the movement, lowering the dumbbells back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Move through a full range of motion for maximum muscle engagement.
2. Maintain a straight back and avoid using momentum during the lift.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersSeatedDumbbellLateralRaise
string-array.item: Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise
A focused shoulder exercise that isolates the lateral deltoids.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing inward.
2. Raise both dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the ground.
3. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid shrugging your shoulders; focus on using your deltoids to lift the weights.
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbows to reduce strain on your joints.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersCableRearDeltFly
string-array.item: Cable Rear Delt Fly
A cable machine exercise that targets the rear deltoids and upper back muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set the cables at shoulder height and grab the handles with a cross-grip (right hand on the left handle, left hand on the right handle).
2. Step back slightly and stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
3. Pull the cables outward and backward, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your arms slightly bent and avoid locking your elbows.
2. Use a controlled motion to avoid relying on momentum.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersBentOverLateralRaise
string-array.item: Bent Over Lateral Raise
A free-weight exercise that targets the rear deltoids and upper back muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other, and bend at the hips to bring your chest parallel to the ground.
2. Lift the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor.
3. Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
2. Avoid using momentum to lift the dumbbells; focus on engaging the rear deltoids.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersBentArmLateralRaise
string-array.item: Bent Arm Lateral Raise
A shoulder isolation exercise that targets the lateral deltoids with reduced leverage for increased focus.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your elbows bent at a 90-degree angle.
2. Lift the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor.
3. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your elbows bent throughout the movement to maintain proper form.
2. Avoid raising the dumbbells above shoulder height to protect your joints.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersCableUprightRow
string-array.item: Cable Upright Row
The Cable Upright Row is a strength exercise that primarily targets the shoulders and traps while engaging the biceps and forearms.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach a straight bar or rope handle to a low pulley on a cable machine.
2. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the bar with an overhand grip.
3. Keep your back straight and chest up as you pull the bar upwards toward your chin.
4. Lead with your elbows, keeping them higher than the bar throughout the movement.
5. Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid excessive swinging or leaning backward.
2. Perform the exercise in a controlled manner to target the muscles effectively.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersFacePull
string-array.item: Face Pull
The Face Pull is an excellent exercise for strengthening the rear delts, traps, and improving shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach a rope handle to a high pulley on a cable machine.
2. Stand facing the machine, holding the ends of the rope with both hands.
3. Step back slightly and pull the rope toward your face, leading with your elbows.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the peak and slowly return to the start.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged and avoid arching your back.
2. Focus on controlled movements for optimal activation.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersHalfKneelingHighCableRowRope
string-array.item: Half Kneeling High Cable Row Rope
The Half Kneeling High Cable Row Rope targets the lats, traps, and biceps while engaging the core for stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set a cable machine to a high pulley and attach a rope handle.
2. Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat on the ground for support.
3. Grasp the rope with both hands and pull it toward your chest, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the peak of the movement.
5. Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a straight back and avoid rotating your torso.
2. Keep the movement slow and controlled for better muscle engagement.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersLeaningCableLateralRaise
string-array.item: Leaning Cable Lateral Raise
The Leaning Cable Lateral Raise is a shoulder isolation exercise that targets the lateral deltoid, helping to build width and definition.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach a handle to the low pulley on a cable machine.
2. Stand sideways to the machine and grab the handle with the arm farthest from the pulley.
3. Lean slightly away from the machine, supporting yourself with your other hand.
4. Raise your arm laterally until it is parallel to the floor.
5. Slowly lower the arm back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum to lift the weight.
2. Keep a slight bend in the elbow throughout the motion.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellRaise
string-array.item: Dumbbell Raise
The Dumbbell Raise is a versatile exercise that can target different parts of the shoulder depending on the angle of the lift.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. With a slight bend in your elbows, raise the dumbbells outward and upward to shoulder level.
3. Pause briefly at the top before lowering the dumbbells back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid swinging the weights or using momentum to lift.
2. Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellUprightRow
string-array.item: Dumbbell Upright Row
The Dumbbell Upright Row targets the shoulders and traps, while also engaging the biceps for assistance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing your thighs.
2. Pull the dumbbells upward along your torso, leading with your elbows.
3. Raise the weights to just below your chin, keeping your elbows higher than your hands.
4. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid swinging the weights or arching your back.
2. Perform the exercise with controlled movements for optimal muscle engagement.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersBodyweightMilitaryPress
string-array.item: Bodyweight Military Press
The Bodyweight Military Press is a challenging shoulder exercise that develops strength and stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a pike push-up position, with your hips elevated and hands shoulder-width apart on the floor.
2. Bend your elbows and lower your head toward the ground in a controlled motion.
3. Push back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
4. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability.
2. Adjust the angle of your body to modify the intensity of the exercise.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersPushPress
string-array.item: Push Press
The Push Press is a compound exercise that builds explosive strength in the shoulders, triceps, and legs.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell or dumbbells at shoulder height.
2. Slightly bend your knees to lower your body into a quarter squat.
3. Drive through your legs and press the weight overhead in one fluid motion.
4. Lower the weight back to shoulder height and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core tight to protect your lower back.
2. Use controlled movements to avoid jerking or losing balance.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersEzBarUprightRow
string-array.item: Ez Bar Upright Row
The Ez Bar Upright Row is a shoulder and upper trap exercise that also engages the biceps and forearms.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright, holding an EZ bar with an overhand grip at hip level.
2. Pull the bar upward along your torso, leading with your elbows.
3. Raise the bar to chest level, keeping your elbows higher than your hands.
4. Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum or excessive swinging.
2. Perform the exercise in a controlled manner to maximize muscle activation.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellLyingOneArmRearLateralRaise
string-array.item: Dumbbell Lying One-Arm Rear Lateral Raise
The Dumbbell Lying One-Arm Rear Lateral Raise isolates the rear delts and upper back muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your side on a flat bench, holding a dumbbell in your top hand.
2. Keep your elbow slightly bent and raise the dumbbell outward and upward to shoulder height.
3. Pause briefly at the top and lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired number of reps before switching sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rotating your torso or using momentum to lift the weight.
2. Focus on slow, controlled movements for better isolation.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersLateralRaiseMachine
string-array.item: Lateral Raise Machine
The Lateral Raise Machine isolates the shoulder\'s lateral deltoid muscles, enhancing shoulder width and definition.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the machine with your arms positioned under the padded levers and your back straight.
2. Grip the handles (if available) or rest your hands lightly on the pads.
3. Push the levers upward by raising your elbows out to the sides.
4. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Adjust the seat height so your elbows align with the machine\'s pivot point.
2. Focus on smooth, controlled motions to avoid jerking.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersScottPress
string-array.item: Scott Press
The Scott Press is a variation of the shoulder press that targets the front and lateral deltoids.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit or stand with a dumbbell in each hand, held at shoulder height with palms facing forward.
2. Press the dumbbells upward in a diagonal path, bringing them closer together at the top.
3. Lower the weights back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your elbows slightly bent throughout the movement.
2. Use a controlled tempo to maintain tension on the deltoids.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersBandPullApart
string-array.item: Band Pull-Apart
The Band Pull-Apart is a simple yet effective exercise for strengthening the rear delts and upper back.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a resistance band with both hands at shoulder height, arms extended forward.
2. Pull the band apart by moving your hands outward until your arms are in line with your torso.
3. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your shoulders down and avoid shrugging.
2. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersBentOverReverseCableFly
string-array.item: Bent Over Reverse Cable Fly
The Bent Over Reverse Cable Fly targets the rear delts and upper back, improving posture and shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set the cable handles to the lowest setting on a dual-cable machine.
2. Bend at the hips with a slight bend in your knees, keeping your back straight.
3. Grab a handle in each hand and pull the cables outward and upward until your arms are in line with your shoulders.
4. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum; focus on controlled movements.
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbows to reduce strain on the joints.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersBentOverBarbellReverseRaise
string-array.item: Bent-Over Barbell Reverse Raise
The Bent-Over Barbell Reverse Raise strengthens the rear delts and traps, contributing to a balanced shoulder appearance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with a pronated grip.
2. Bend at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the ground, keeping your back straight.
3. Raise the barbell outward and upward, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
4. Lower the barbell back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rounding your back during the movement.
2. Perform the exercise with slow, controlled motions for optimal effectiveness.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersWeightedRoundArm
string-array.item: Weighted Round Arm
The Weighted Round Arm exercise strengthens the shoulders, biceps, and triceps while improving arm mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or weight plate in each hand.
2. Extend your arms forward and trace a large circular motion, moving the weights around in a smooth, controlled arc.
3. Complete the circle and reverse the direction for the next repetition.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your movements smooth to avoid jerking.
2. Use a light weight to maintain control and proper form.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersWeightPlateFrontRaise
string-array.item: Weight Plate Front Raise
The Weight Plate Front Raise isolates the anterior deltoids for building shoulder strength and size.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright, holding a weight plate with both hands at the 3 o’clock and 9 o’clock positions.
2. Keep your arms straight and lift the plate until it reaches shoulder height.
3. Lower the plate back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid swinging the weight to maintain focus on the shoulders.
2. Keep your core engaged for stability.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersTwoArmCableLateralRaise
string-array.item: Two Arm Cable Lateral Raise
The Two Arm Cable Lateral Raise targets the lateral deltoids, enhancing shoulder width and definition.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set the cables to the lowest position on a dual-cable machine and hold the handles with your arms at your sides.
2. Raise your arms laterally until they are parallel to the ground.
3. Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep a slight bend in your elbows to reduce joint strain.
2. Use controlled movements to prevent momentum from taking over.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersLandmineSquatToPress
string-array.item: Landmine Squat to Press
The Landmine Squat to Press combines a squat and overhead press, targeting the legs, shoulders, and core.
To perform the exercise:
1. Place one end of a barbell into a landmine attachment or secure it in a corner.
2. Hold the barbell near the weighted end with both hands at chest level.
3. Perform a squat, then as you stand up, press the barbell overhead.
4. Lower the barbell back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to maintain balance.
2. Avoid leaning forward during the squat phase.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersCableShoulderPress
string-array.item: Cable Shoulder Press
The Cable Shoulder Press builds shoulder strength while providing constant tension throughout the movement.
To perform the exercise:
1. Adjust the cables to shoulder height and attach handles to each side.
2. Hold the handles at shoulder level with your palms facing forward.
3. Press the handles upward until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the handles back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your elbows slightly in front of your body for a natural pressing path.
2. Avoid arching your back by keeping your core engaged.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersBarbellRearDeltRaise
string-array.item: Barbell Rear Delt Raise
The Barbell Rear Delt Raise targets the rear deltoids and upper back muscles for improved posture and shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a barbell with a pronated grip and stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the ground.
3. With a slight bend in your elbows, raise the barbell outward until your arms are parallel to the floor.
4. Lower the barbell back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum by performing slow, controlled movements.
2. Keep your core engaged to protect your lower back.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDoubleCableFrontRaise
string-array.item: Double Cable Front Raise
The Double Cable Front Raise isolates the front deltoids for shoulder strength and size.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set the cables to the lowest position on a dual-cable machine and hold the handles with your arms at your sides.
2. With your palms facing down, raise the cables forward until your arms are at shoulder height.
3. Lower the cables back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep a slight bend in your elbows to reduce joint strain.
2. Avoid leaning back during the movement; maintain a neutral spine.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersStandingSmithMachineShoulderPress
string-array.item: Standing Smith Machine Shoulder Press
The Standing Smith Machine Shoulder Press strengthens the shoulders and triceps while providing stability for controlled pressing.
To perform the exercise:
1. Position the bar of the Smith machine at shoulder height.
2. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grip the bar with your palms facing forward.
3. Press the bar upward until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the bar back to shoulder level and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid locking your elbows at the top to maintain tension on the muscles.
2. Keep your core engaged to stabilize your body.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellWPress
string-array.item: Dumbbell W Press
The Dumbbell W Press strengthens the shoulders and improves mobility by engaging multiple shoulder muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms bent and palms facing forward.
2. Start with your elbows in line with your shoulders, forming a "W" shape with your arms.
3. Press the dumbbells upward and outward, fully extending your arms.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to the "W" position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your movements controlled to avoid swinging the weights.
2. Focus on maintaining the "W" shape throughout the exercise.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellOneArmShoulderPress
string-array.item: Dumbbell One Arm Shoulder Press
The Dumbbell One Arm Shoulder Press targets shoulder stability and strength while engaging the core for balance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in one hand at shoulder height with your palm facing forward.
2. Press the dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended.
3. Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core tight to prevent leaning to one side.
2. Perform equal repetitions on each side for balanced development.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellScaption
string-array.item: Dumbbell Scaption
The Dumbbell Scaption targets the stabilizing muscles of the shoulders, focusing on the rotator cuff and deltoids.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms resting at your sides, palms facing inward.
2. Raise your arms at a 30-degree angle to the front until they are at shoulder height.
3. Lower your arms back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use light weights to avoid straining the shoulder joint.
2. Keep your movements controlled and avoid swinging the dumbbells.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersBarbellCleanAndPress
string-array.item: Barbell Clean and Press
The Barbell Clean and Press is a full-body exercise that builds explosive power, strength, and coordination.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and a barbell on the ground in front of you.
2. Perform a clean by lifting the bar to your shoulders in one fluid motion.
3. Press the barbell overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the bar back to your shoulders, then to the ground, and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core and maintain a straight back throughout the movement.
2. Start with a manageable weight to perfect your form before progressing.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellCubanPress
string-array.item: Dumbbell Cuban Press
The Dumbbell Cuban Press combines shoulder rotation and pressing to strengthen the rotator cuff and deltoids.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lift your arms so your elbows are at shoulder height and bent at 90 degrees.
2. Rotate your forearms upward to bring the dumbbells overhead.
3. Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended.
4. Reverse the motion back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use light to moderate weights to avoid compromising form.
2. Focus on smooth, controlled movements to engage the targeted muscles.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellCubanExternalRotation
string-array.item: Dumbbell Cuban External Rotation
The Dumbbell Cuban External Rotation improves shoulder stability and strengthens the rotator cuff.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your elbows bent at 90 degrees and at shoulder height.
2. Rotate your forearms upward and outward while keeping your elbows in place.
3. Lower your forearms back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your movements controlled and avoid using momentum.
2. Focus on maintaining proper posture to target the correct muscles.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersStandingAlternatingDumbbellShoulderPress
string-array.item: Standing Alternating Dumbbell Shoulder Press
The Standing Alternating Dumbbell Shoulder Press strengthens the shoulders and core while promoting balance and stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing forward.
2. Press one dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended.
3. Lower the dumbbell back to shoulder height and repeat with the opposite arm.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid leaning or twisting during the exercise; keep your core engaged.
2. Perform the movement slowly to maximize muscle engagement.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersCableExternalShoulderRotation
string-array.item: Cable External Shoulder Rotation
The Cable External Shoulder Rotation targets the rotator cuff and improves shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach a single handle to a low cable pulley and stand perpendicular to the machine.
2. Hold the handle with the arm closest to the machine, elbow bent at 90 degrees, and upper arm close to your side.
3. Rotate your forearm outward while keeping your elbow fixed in place.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use light weight to focus on controlled movement.
2. Avoid letting your elbow move away from your body.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersCableInternalShoulderRotation
string-array.item: Cable Internal Shoulder Rotation
The Cable Internal Shoulder Rotation strengthens the internal rotators of the shoulder for better joint stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach a single handle to a low cable pulley and stand perpendicular to the machine.
2. Hold the handle with the arm farthest from the machine, elbow bent at 90 degrees, and upper arm close to your side.
3. Rotate your forearm inward across your body while keeping your elbow fixed in place.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Perform the movement slowly and with control.
2. Use a light weight to prevent strain on the shoulder joint.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersAcrossChestShoulderStretch
string-array.item: Across Chest Shoulder Stretch
The Across Chest Shoulder Stretch helps to loosen the shoulder and upper back muscles.
To perform the stretch:
1. Extend one arm across your chest and hold it with your opposite hand just above the elbow.
2. Gently pull your arm closer to your chest until you feel a stretch in your shoulder.
3. Hold the position for 15–30 seconds, then switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rotating your torso; keep it facing forward.
2. Do not apply excessive force; the stretch should feel comfortable.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersStandingReachUpBackRotationStretch
string-array.item: Standing Reach Up Back Rotation Stretch
The Standing Reach Up Back Rotation Stretch improves shoulder mobility and posture.
To perform the stretch:
1. Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Raise one arm overhead and reach backward as far as comfortable.
3. Rotate your upper body slightly in the same direction to deepen the stretch.
4. Hold for 15–30 seconds and switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid hyperextending your lower back.
2. Keep your movements controlled and within a comfortable range.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersShoulderStretchBehindBack
string-array.item: Shoulder Stretch Behind Back
The Shoulder Stretch Behind Back helps to open the shoulders and chest while relieving tension.
To perform the stretch:
1. Stand tall and clasp your hands behind your back, palms facing each other.
2. Straighten your arms and lift them slightly upward while keeping your chest open.
3. Hold the position for 15–30 seconds.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid hunching your shoulders; keep them down and relaxed.
2. If clasping your hands is difficult, use a towel or strap to assist.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersInclineDumbbellSideLateralRaise
string-array.item: Incline Dumbbell Side Lateral Raise
The Incline Dumbbell Side Lateral Raise targets the lateral deltoids, enhancing shoulder width and definition.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set an incline bench at a 30–45-degree angle and lie on your side, holding a dumbbell in your top hand.
2. Start with the dumbbell close to your hip and your arm slightly bent.
3. Raise the dumbbell outward until your arm is parallel to the floor.
4. Lower it back down with control and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use a light weight to maintain good form.
2. Avoid using momentum to lift the dumbbell.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellSideLyingRearDeltRaise
string-array.item: Dumbbell Side Lying Rear Delt Raise
The Dumbbell Side Lying Rear Delt Raise isolates the rear deltoids, improving upper back and shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your side on a flat bench or the floor, holding a dumbbell in your top hand.
2. Keep your arm slightly bent and start with the dumbbell in front of your body.
3. Raise the dumbbell upward in an arc until it’s level with your shoulder.
4. Lower it back down and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Focus on slow, controlled movements.
2. Keep your torso stable and avoid twisting.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersLyingCableReverseFly
string-array.item: Lying Cable Reverse Fly
The Lying Cable Reverse Fly targets the rear delts and upper back muscles for improved posture and strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on a bench placed between two low cable pulleys.
2. Hold the cable handles in each hand with your arms extended downward.
3. Raise your arms outward in a wide arc until they are level with your shoulders.
4. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use a light weight to ensure smooth, controlled movement.
2. Avoid shrugging your shoulders during the lift.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersSingleArmCircles
string-array.item: Single Arm Circles
Single Arm Circles are a dynamic warm-up exercise that mobilizes the shoulder joint and improves flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Extend one arm straight out to the side and begin making small circles with your hand.
3. Gradually increase the circle size for a greater range of motion.
4. Reverse the direction after a few seconds and switch arms.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your arm straight but relaxed.
2. Maintain a steady pace to avoid jerking movements.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellLateralToFrontRaise
string-array.item: Dumbbell Lateral to Front Raise
The Dumbbell Lateral to Front Raise combines lateral and front raises to work the deltoids and improve shoulder definition.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright, holding dumbbells at your sides with your palms facing inward.
2. Lift the dumbbells outward to shoulder height, forming a T-shape with your body.
3. Bring the dumbbells in front of you at shoulder height, then lower them back down.
4. Reverse the movement to return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use controlled movements to avoid swinging the weights.
2. Keep your core engaged to maintain proper posture.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersOneArmBentOverCableLateralRaise
string-array.item: One-Arm Bent Over Cable Lateral Raise
The One-Arm Bent Over Cable Lateral Raise targets the rear deltoids and upper back, enhancing shoulder stability and strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set a cable pulley to the lowest position and attach a single handle.
2. Stand to the side of the cable machine and bend forward at the hips, keeping your back flat.
3. Grab the handle with the hand furthest from the machine, arm extended downward.
4. Raise your arm outward until it is parallel to the floor, then lower back down with control.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your torso stable and avoid twisting.
2. Use a light weight to maintain good form.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersHandstandPushUp
string-array.item: Handstand Push-Up
The Handstand Push-Up is a challenging bodyweight exercise that builds shoulder, arm, and core strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Kick up into a handstand position against a wall for support.
2. Lower your head toward the ground in a controlled motion, keeping your elbows tucked slightly inward.
3. Push back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core to maintain balance.
2. Use a spotter or wall for stability if you\'re a beginner.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersEZBarUnderhandPress
string-array.item: EZ Bar Underhand Press
The EZ Bar Underhand Press strengthens the anterior deltoids and triceps while reducing wrist strain.
To perform the exercise:
1. Grip the EZ bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Start with the bar at chest level and press it upward until your arms are fully extended.
3. Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your wrists straight to avoid unnecessary strain.
2. Maintain a steady, controlled motion throughout the exercise.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellLyingExternalShoulderRotation
string-array.item: Dumbbell Lying External Shoulder Rotation
The Dumbbell Lying External Shoulder Rotation targets the rotator cuff, improving shoulder stability and injury prevention.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your side on a flat bench or floor, holding a dumbbell in the hand of the upper arm.
2. Bend your elbow to a 90-degree angle, keeping it close to your side.
3. Rotate your forearm upward as far as comfortably possible, then lower it back down.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use a light weight to avoid overloading the rotator cuff.
2. Focus on slow, controlled movements for effectiveness.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersInclineDumbbellReverseFly
string-array.item: Incline Dumbbell Reverse Fly
The Incline Dumbbell Reverse Fly strengthens the rear deltoids and upper back muscles, promoting posture and balance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set an incline bench to a 30–45-degree angle and lie face down on it, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Start with your arms hanging straight down, palms facing each other.
3. Raise your arms outward in a wide arc until they are parallel to the floor.
4. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum to lift the weights.
2. Keep your chest on the bench to isolate the target muscles.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersInclineDumbbellYRaise
string-array.item: Incline Dumbbell Y-Raise
The Incline Dumbbell Y-Raise targets the upper back and rear deltoids, improving posture and shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set an incline bench to a 30–45-degree angle and lie face down on it, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Let your arms hang straight down, palms facing each other.
3. Raise your arms upward at an angle, forming a "Y" shape, until they are in line with your body.
4. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use a controlled motion and avoid swinging the weights.
2. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellInclineTRaise
string-array.item: Dumbbell Incline T-Raise
The Dumbbell Incline T-Raise works the rear deltoids, traps, and rhomboids, enhancing upper back strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on an incline bench set at a 30–45-degree angle, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Start with your arms hanging straight down, palms facing each other.
3. Raise your arms outward to the sides, forming a "T" shape, until they are parallel to the floor.
4. Lower the dumbbells back down with control and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your movements smooth and controlled.
2. Avoid shrugging your shoulders during the lift.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersBenchSupportedDumbbellExternalRotation
string-array.item: Bench Supported Dumbbell External Rotation
This exercise targets the rotator cuff, enhancing shoulder stability and mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set an incline bench to a low angle and lie on it sideways, supporting your upper body.
2. Hold a dumbbell in the hand of the upper arm, with your elbow bent at 90 degrees and supported against your side.
3. Rotate your forearm upward, keeping your elbow fixed, then slowly return to the start position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use light weights to prevent straining the rotator cuff.
2. Perform the motion slowly to maintain control and precision.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellSeatedBentOverRearDeltRow
string-array.item: Dumbbell Seated Bent Over Rear Delt Row
This exercise strengthens the rear deltoids, traps, and upper back muscles, improving posture and stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground, holding dumbbells in each hand.
2. Bend forward at the hips, letting the dumbbells hang below your shoulders.
3. Pull the dumbbells up and outward, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Slowly lower the dumbbells back down and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight to avoid strain.
2. Focus on using your rear delts rather than momentum to lift the weights.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellStandingPalmsInPress
string-array.item: Dumbbell Standing Palms In Press
This exercise focuses on shoulder and tricep strength while minimizing stress on the shoulder joint.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright, holding dumbbells in each hand with your palms facing each other.
2. Start with the dumbbells at shoulder height, elbows bent.
3. Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the dumbbells back down to shoulder height and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to maintain balance.
2. Avoid flaring your elbows out excessively during the press.

string-array.name: descriptionLyingShoulderPress
string-array.item: Lying Shoulder Press
The Lying Shoulder Press is an upper body exercise that primarily targets the deltoid muscles while also engaging the triceps and upper chest.
This variation is performed on an incline bench to isolate the shoulders and reduce strain on the lower back compared to standing versions.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set an incline bench to 45-60 degrees and lie back with dumbbells
2. Hold the weights at shoulder level with palms facing forward
3. Press the weights upward until arms are fully extended
4. Slowly lower back to the starting position
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a slight bend in elbows at the top position
2. Keep your core engaged throughout the movement
3. Avoid arching your lower back during the press
4. Use a spotter when attempting heavy weights

string-array.name: descriptionDumbbellRearDeltRow
string-array.item: Dumbbell Rear Delt Row
The Dumbbell Rear Delt Row specifically targets the posterior deltoid muscles to improve shoulder balance and posture.
This exercise helps counteract rounded shoulders by strengthening the often-neglected rear delts.
To perform the exercise:
1. Bend forward at 45 degrees holding dumbbells with palms facing
2. Pull the weights up and out to 90-degree angles
3. Squeeze shoulder blades together at the top position
4. Slowly lower back to starting position
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a neutral spine throughout
2. Focus on muscle contraction rather than heavy weight
3. Imagine pouring water from your elbows at the top
4. Keep movements slow and controlled

string-array.name: descriptionLeverLateralRaise
string-array.item: Lever Lateral Raise
The Lever Lateral Raise isolates the medial deltoids using specialized gym equipment for balanced shoulder development.
This machine variation provides constant tension throughout the movement range.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit in the machine with arms at your sides
2. Lift arms upward to shoulder height
3. Maintain a slight bend in elbows
4. Slowly lower back to starting position
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid shrugging your shoulders upward
2. Keep wrists neutral throughout
3. Focus on 2-second lift, 3-second lower tempo
4. Use weight that allows perfect form

string-array.name: descriptionKettlebellOneArmMilitaryPress
string-array.item: Kettlebell One-Arm Military Press
This overhead pressing variation builds shoulder strength and stability with unilateral loading.
The kettlebell\'s offset center of gravity increases core engagement and shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Clean the kettlebell to rack position
2. Press overhead while keeping wrist straight
3. Fully extend arm without hyperextending elbow
4. Lower with control back to rack position
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep ribs down to avoid excessive arch
2. Brace your core throughout movement
3. Maintain neutral head position
4. Complete all reps on one side before switching

string-array.name: descriptionKettlebellSplitSnatch
string-array.item: Kettlebell Split Snatch
This explosive movement develops power, coordination, and shoulder mobility.
The split stance variation adds stability while training full-body coordination.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in athletic stance with kettlebell between legs
2. Explosively extend hips while pulling kettlebell up
3. Drop into split stance as bell flips overhead
4. Stand up with bell locked out overhead
Tips for proper execution:
1. Focus on powerful hip drive initiation
2. Keep arm relaxed during the pull phase
3. Punch upward to secure lockout position
4. Practice with light weight to master technique

string-array.name: descriptionKettlebellWindmill
string-array.item: Kettlebell Windmill
The Kettlebell Windmill is a dynamic exercise that improves shoulder mobility, core stability, and hip hinge mechanics.
This compound movement challenges full-body coordination while working on flexibility and strength simultaneously.
To perform the exercise:
1. Press one kettlebell overhead and lock out your arm
2. Stagger your feet slightly with toes pointed outward
3. Hinge at hips while keeping eyes on the kettlebell
4. Lower opposite hand toward foot while maintaining overhead lockout
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your eyes on the kettlebell throughout
2. Maintain a locked elbow on the loaded side
3. Move slowly with complete control
4. Start with very light weight to learn the movement pattern

string-array.name: descriptionKettlebellSwings
string-array.item: Kettlebell Swings
The Kettlebell Swing is a fundamental explosive exercise that develops power in the posterior chain.
This movement teaches proper hip hinge mechanics while building endurance and power.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, kettlebell between legs
2. Hinge at hips and swing kettlebell back between legs
3. Explosively extend hips to propel kettlebell forward
4. Control the descent for the next repetition
Tips for proper execution:
1. Drive the movement with your hips, not your arms
2. Keep your core braced throughout
3. The kettlebell should reach chest height at peak
4. Avoid squatting - focus on the hip hinge motion

string-array.name: descriptionKettlebellArnoldPress
string-array.item: Kettlebell Arnold Press
The Kettlebell Arnold Press is a rotational overhead press that works all three deltoid heads.
This variation adds grip challenge and core activation compared to dumbbell version.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold kettlebells in rack position with palms facing you
2. Begin pressing while rotating palms outward
3. At full extension, palms should face forward
4. Reverse the motion on the way down
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain neutral wrist position
2. Control the rotation throughout
3. Avoid excessive arching in lower back
4. Use moderate weight to maintain proper form

string-array.name: descriptionBentOverRearDeltFlyGymstick
string-array.item: Bent Over Rear Delt Fly | Gymstick
This variation using the Gymstick specifically targets the rear deltoids with adjustable resistance.
The flexible bar provides progressive tension for optimal muscle engagement.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand on center of Gymstick with feet shoulder-width
2. Hinge forward 45 degrees holding the handles
3. Lift arms outward to shoulder height
4. Slowly return to starting position
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain slight bend in elbows
2. Squeeze shoulder blades at peak contraction
3. Control resistance on the lowering phase
4. Adjust foot position to modify resistance

string-array.name: descriptionCableSeatedShoulderInternalRotation
string-array.item: Cable Seated Shoulder Internal Rotation
This rotator cuff exercise strengthens the internal rotators for shoulder health and balance.
It helps prevent imbalances that can lead to shoulder impingement issues.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit sideways to cable machine with elbow bent 90°
2. Keep elbow tucked at your side throughout
3. Rotate forearm inward across your body
4. Slowly return to starting position
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use very light weight - focus on control
2. Maintain proper elbow position
3. Perform equal reps on both sides
4. Combine with external rotation exercises

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersHalfKneelingCableExternalRotation
string-array.item: Half Kneeling Cable External Rotation
This exercise strengthens the external rotator muscles of the shoulder, improving stability and preventing injury.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set the cable handle at elbow height while kneeling sideways to the machine with the outside knee down.
2. Hold the cable handle with the hand furthest from the machine, keeping your elbow bent at 90 degrees and tucked into your side.
3. Rotate your forearm outward until it is perpendicular to your body.
4. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid shrugging your shoulder; keep it relaxed and down.
2. Perform the movement in a slow and controlled manner.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersLandmineLateralRaise
string-array.item: Landmine Lateral Raise
This exercise targets the lateral deltoids, improving shoulder width and strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Secure one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or corner of a wall.
2. Stand sideways to the barbell, holding the free end with the hand furthest from it.
3. Raise the barbell laterally until your arm reaches shoulder height.
4. Lower the barbell back down and repeat for the desired repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning to the side.
2. Use controlled movements to engage the target muscles effectively.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersSeatedDumbbellFrontRaise
string-array.item: Seated Dumbbell Front Raise
The Seated Dumbbell Front Raise targets the front deltoids, improving shoulder strength and size.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms resting by your sides.
2. Raise the dumbbells to shoulder height in front of you, keeping your arms straight.
3. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid swinging the weights; focus on controlled movements.
2. Keep your core engaged to maintain stability.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersScapularProtractionAndRetraction
string-array.item: Scapular Protraction and Retraction
This exercise improves scapular mobility and shoulder blade control, enhancing overall shoulder function.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand or sit with your arms extended forward at shoulder height.
2. Push your hands forward to protract your shoulder blades, then retract them by pulling your shoulder blades back together.
3. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep the movement focused on the shoulder blades, avoiding excessive arm movement.
2. Maintain a neutral spine throughout the exercise.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersOneArmKettlebellSnatch
string-array.item: One Arm Kettlebell Snatch
This explosive exercise targets the shoulders, back, and core, improving power and coordination.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell with one hand between your legs.
2. Drive through your hips to swing the kettlebell upward, pulling it close to your body.
3. At the top, rotate your hand and lock out the kettlebell overhead.
4. Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use your hips and legs for power, not just your arm.
2. Keep the kettlebell path close to your body for better control.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersCrossCableFacePull
string-array.item: Cross Cable Face Pull
This exercise targets the rear deltoids, traps, and upper back, promoting better posture and shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set the pulleys on a cable machine at upper chest level and attach rope handles to each side.
2. Cross the cables so the left hand holds the right handle and the right hand holds the left handle.
3. Pull the handles toward your face, keeping your elbows high and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning back.
2. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades at the peak of the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersOneArmLandmineRow
string-array.item: One Arm Landmine Row
This exercise targets the lats, traps, and rhomboids, building upper back strength and improving shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Place one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or secure it in a corner.
2. Stand on the opposite side of the barbell with your feet staggered and the front hand holding the free end.
3. Row the barbell towards your waist, squeezing your shoulder blade at the top.
4. Slowly lower it back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged and back straight throughout the movement.
2. Avoid shrugging your shoulders or twisting your torso.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersResistanceBandSeatedShoulderPress
string-array.item: Resistance Band Seated Shoulder Press
This exercise strengthens the shoulders and improves stability using resistance bands.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and a resistance band looped under them.
2. Hold the band handles at shoulder level with palms facing forward.
3. Press the handles upward until your arms are fully extended.
4. Slowly lower the handles back to shoulder level and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Move in a controlled manner to maintain tension in the bands.
2. Keep your core tight to stabilize your torso.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersBenchPikePushUp
string-array.item: Bench Pike Push-Up
This bodyweight exercise targets the shoulders, particularly the anterior deltoids, as well as the triceps and core.
To perform the exercise:
1. Place your feet on a bench and hands on the floor in a pike position, with hips elevated and arms straight.
2. Bend your elbows to lower your head toward the floor.
3. Push back up to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and avoid arching your lower back.
2. Lower your head gently to prevent neck strain.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersPikePushUp
string-array.item: Pike Push-Up
The Pike Push-Up builds shoulder strength and is a precursor to handstand push-ups.
To perform the exercise:
1. Begin in a downward dog position with hands and feet on the floor, hips elevated.
2. Lower your head toward the floor by bending your elbows.
3. Push back up to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged and back straight.
2. Use a slow, controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersTallKneelingOneArmKettlebellPress
string-array.item: Tall Kneeling One Arm Kettlebell Press
This exercise targets the shoulders and core, improving stability and unilateral strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Kneel on the floor in a tall kneeling position with your hips extended and glutes engaged.
2. Hold a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height with the bell resting on the back of your wrist.
3. Press the kettlebell straight overhead until your arm is fully extended.
4. Slowly lower it back to shoulder height and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core tight to avoid arching your lower back.
2. Move in a controlled manner to maintain balance and stability.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersKettlebellCleanAndJerk
string-array.item: Kettlebell Clean and Jerk
This full-body exercise focuses on explosive power, targeting the shoulders, legs, and core.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start with the kettlebell on the ground in front of you, gripping the handle with one hand.
2. Perform a clean to bring the kettlebell to shoulder height in a rack position.
3. Quickly dip and drive through your legs to press the kettlebell overhead.
4. Lower the kettlebell back to the rack position and then to the ground to repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Focus on explosive hip drive during the clean.
2. Avoid letting the kettlebell crash onto your wrist; keep the movement smooth.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersFullRangeOfMotionLatPulldown
string-array.item: Full Range of Motion Lat Pulldown
This exercise targets the lats and improves overall upper body strength and posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit at a lat pulldown machine with the bar attached to the cable above you.
2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with your palms facing away.
3. Pull the bar down to your chest while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Slowly release the bar back to the starting position with full arm extension.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum; focus on controlled movements.
2. Keep your torso upright and engage your core throughout.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersLeverShoulderPressHammerGrip
string-array.item: Lever Shoulder Press (Hammer Grip)
This exercise targets the deltoid muscles, focusing on strength and hypertrophy.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the lever shoulder press machine and grip the handles with a neutral (hammer) grip.
2. Press the handles upward until your arms are fully extended without locking your elbows.
3. Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back pressed against the seat for support.
2. Avoid using excessive weight to ensure proper form.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersDumbbellLyingRearLateralRaise
string-array.item: Dumbbell Lying Rear Lateral Raise
This exercise isolates the rear deltoids, improving shoulder stability and posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on an incline bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging down.
2. Raise the dumbbells out to the sides until they are level with your shoulders.
3. Slowly lower them back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
2. Avoid swinging the weights; focus on controlled movements.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersLeverReverseShoulderPress
string-array.item: Lever Reverse Shoulder Press
This exercise emphasizes the rear deltoids and upper back muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit facing the lever shoulder press machine, gripping the handles with palms facing inward.
2. Press the handles away from your body until your arms are fully extended.
3. Slowly return the handles to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the movement.
2. Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the press.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersSideLyingRearDeltDumbbellRaise
string-array.item: Side Lying Rear Delt Dumbbell Raise
This isolation exercise targets the rear deltoids for improved shoulder stability and posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your side on a bench or the floor, holding a dumbbell in your top hand.
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbow and raise the dumbbell out to the side until it is level with your shoulder.
3. Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Perform the movement slowly to maintain control and focus on the target muscle.
2. Avoid rotating your torso during the lift.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersScapulaDips
string-array.item: Scapula Dips
This exercise strengthens the scapular stabilizers, improving shoulder health and mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Position yourself on parallel bars with your arms straight and shoulders relaxed.
2. Without bending your elbows, lower your body by allowing your shoulders to move up.
3. Push your shoulders down to lift your body slightly and return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Focus on the movement of your scapulae rather than your arms.
2. Keep your core engaged to maintain stability.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersEzBarInclineFrontRaise
string-array.item: Ez-Bar Incline Front Raise
This exercise targets the front deltoids, enhancing shoulder strength and definition.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on an incline bench while holding an EZ bar with a shoulder-width grip.
2. Raise the bar in front of you to shoulder height, keeping your arms straight.
3. Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core tight and avoid arching your back.
2. Move in a controlled manner to prevent momentum from assisting the lift.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersBackLever
string-array.item: Back Lever
This advanced bodyweight exercise targets the shoulders, back, and core, requiring significant strength and stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hang from a bar with an overhand grip and bring your legs up to a tucked position.
2. Straighten your body horizontally, keeping your core tight and arms locked.
3. Hold the position for a few seconds, then return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Practice progressions like tuck holds before attempting the full movement.
2. Engage your entire body to maintain stability and control.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersBarbellFrontRaiseTwist
string-array.item: Barbell Front Raise Twist
This exercise targets the front deltoids and adds rotational movement for core engagement.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a barbell with both hands at shoulder-width grip in front of your thighs.
2. Raise the barbell to shoulder height while simultaneously twisting it slightly to one side.
3. Lower the barbell back to the starting position and repeat, alternating the twist direction.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to stabilize your body.
2. Avoid using momentum; perform the movement in a controlled manner.

string-array.name: descriptionShouldersKettlebellShoulderPress
string-array.item: Kettlebell Shoulder Press
This exercise targets the shoulders, focusing on strength and stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height with your palm facing inward.
2. Press the kettlebell overhead until your arm is fully extended.
